```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 8
    n_vehicles = 4
    Q = 50  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[76, 79], [27, 28], [67, 63], [42, 85], [61, 40], [70, 76], [16, 52], [52, 95]]
    demands = [17, 12, 13, 25, 14, 5, 24, 5]
    time_windows = [[0, 298], [41, 103], [41, 115], [40, 139], [56, 137], [28, 86], [31, 85], [52, 112], [45, 115]]
    service_times = [12, 14, 6, 12, 9, 11, 13, 10]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Memo: Delivery Routing and Scheduling Challenge

Overview
We will execute a same-day delivery operation from a central depot to a set of customers, each with a defined delivery time window. All vehicles are identical and will depart the depot at time 0. Each vehicle will make a single trip—leave the depot at the start, visit an assigned sequence of customers, and return to the depot before the end of the planning horizon. Travel time between any two locations is taken as the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with distance and time measured in the same units.

Challenge
The core planning task is to determine:
- Which customers each vehicle will serve
- The order in which each vehicle will visit its assigned customers
- The timing of service at each stop, including any waiting when arriving early
All customers must be visited exactly once during the day. The plan must be both feasible (meeting capacity and time constraints) and efficient (cost-effective in terms of distance traveled and vehicles deployed).

Key Operating Rules
- Single trip per vehicle: Each vehicle departs the depot at time 0, completes its route, and returns before the depot closes. No mid-day returns or second trips.
- Time windows at customers: Service must begin within each customer’s earliest and latest acceptable delivery time. If a vehicle arrives before a window opens, it waits on site until service can start.
- Service duration: Each stop requires a specific unloading/service time. A vehicle departs a customer once that service time has elapsed.
- Capacity management: The total load on any vehicle at any time must not exceed its capacity. No split deliveries; each customer’s full demand is delivered by exactly one vehicle.
- Travel time and distance: Moving between locations uses straight-line distance. With unit speed, one unit of distance equals one unit of time for planning purposes.
- Cost of deployment: Putting a vehicle into service incurs a fixed cost in addition to distance-based travel cost. Plans that use more vehicles than necessary will face higher fixed costs.

Goal
Develop a set of vehicle routes that:
- Visit every customer exactly once
- Respect all customer time windows and service times
- Keep vehicle loads within capacity on every segment of every route
- Ensure all vehicles return to the depot before closing time
- Minimize total travel distance plus the fixed deployment costs of the vehicles used

Expected Planning Outputs
- A route plan for each vehicle (sequence of stops, including the depot return)
- Arrival, start-of-service, and departure times at each stop
- Load progression along each route to confirm capacity compliance
- A summary of the total distance traveled and the number of vehicles used, with the associated total cost
